title: VoxDose 2.0: scientific vocal dose analysis

creators.name: Cruz, Tiago Lima Bicalho
creators.affiliation: Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG), Brazil

description:
VoxDose is scientific software for vocal dose analysis, comparisons of long recordings, and descriptive self-reports of vocal effort and fatigue.

Original MATLAB dosimetry code: Pasquale Bottalico. VoxDose adaptation, development and modernization: Tiago Lima Bicalho Cruz, Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG), Brazil. Bottalico's contributor credit identifies the original code contribution, separately from the new VoxDose implementation. The dose framework is based on Titze, Svec and Popolo (2003).

Revision 2.0.2 provides a tabbed PySide6 application, English defaults and Brazilian Portuguese selection, immediate hover help, block processing, comparison of long recordings, a descriptive diary, Excel/CSV/PNG/SVG exports, and a single-file Windows executable and NSIS installer with both illustrated manuals. A native macOS builder is included, but Mac binaries have not been generated or validated.

The current regression suite contains 53 tests. Recorded Windows delivery passed three executable rounds (53 source tests and 45 application checks per round) and three NSIS install/launch/uninstall cycles. Independent synthetic ground-truth testing met 142 of 144 acceptance criteria; two F0 precision criteria at SNR 10 dB remain unmet. These computational checks do not establish clinical validity or universal vocal-fatigue thresholds.

The repository's existing non-commercial license is preserved. See the LICENSE file for the actual terms; this record's Other (Non-Commercial) category does not replace that license. Third-party authorship and licenses remain applicable.
